name: Sinus Pericranii

criteria.description: Presence of a soft, compressible, non-pulsatile scalp swelling that increases in size with Valsalva maneuver or head dependency
Radiologic evidence of abnormal communication between extracranial venous structures and intracranial dural venous sinuses on MRI, CT venography, or conventional angiography
Exclusion of other vascular anomalies such as arteriovenous malformations or hemangiomas

diagnosticCriteria.minimumForDiagnosis: Presence of characteristic clinical swelling plus imaging confirmation of venous communication
diagnosticCriteria.notes: Diagnosis is primarily clinical supported by imaging; biopsy is generally avoided due to bleeding risk.

pathognomonic.symptomName: Soft, compressible scalp swelling overlying a venous sinus
pathognomonic.notes: Typically located on the midline or parietal region

pathognomonic.symptomName: Size fluctuation of scalp swelling with Valsalva maneuver or head dependency
pathognomonic.notes: Swelling enlarges when venous pressure increases
searchTerms: scalp swelling changes size with straining
lump size varies with position or Valsalva

common.symptomName: Localized headache adjacent to the lesion
searchTerms: pain in scalp area near swelling

common.symptomName: Visible venous distension over the scalp swelling
common.notes: Dilated veins may be seen radiating from the lesion

common.symptomName: Tenderness on palpation of the swelling
Cosmetic deformity due to scalp swelling
searchTerms: head shape changes due to swelling

occasional.notes: May be related to venous congestion

occasional.symptomName: Mild scalp erythema overlying the lesion
occasional.notes: Usually absent unless secondary inflammation occurs
searchTerms: mild redness on scalp over lesion

occasional.notes: Rarely audible due to venous flow

occasional.symptomName: Mild local edema around the swelling

rare.notes: Very rare, may occur if venous drainage is compromised
searchTerms: headache and vision changes from intracranial hypertension

rare.notes: Extremely rare, possibly due to cortical irritation

imaging: MRI showing extracranial venous sac communicating with intracranial dural venous sinuses
Conventional angiography confirming venous communication without arterial involvement
other: Physical examination revealing compressible scalp swelling with size variation on Valsalva maneuver

distinguishingFeatures: Venous angiomas lack extracranial venous communication
Presence of pulsatile mass with bruit

redFlags: Neurological deficits such as seizures or focal weakness
Signs of intracranial hypertension (e.g., persistent headache, papilledema)
references: Alperovich M, et al. Sinus pericranii: clinical features and management. Neurosurg Focus. 2015;39(4):E7.
Rodesch G, et al. Sinus pericranii: clinical and radiological features. Childs Nerv Syst. 2000;16(10-11):711-7.
